claude.rationale: The deal was a reverse triangular merger in which the whole ESL entity, including its three operating segments, was acquired intact and became a wholly owned TransDigm subsidiary with no segment carve-outs at closing (DEFM14A p.31, structural summary pp.1,30-31); thus the customer-facing products (T4) and the operational processes/segments that produce them (T5) crossed the ownership boundary together as one intact entity, so gap_45 = 0. Likewise the operating processes moved intact alongside the workforce, with the merger agreement binding TransDigm to preserve continuing-employee compensation, benefits, and service credit for one year and requiring ESL to preserve its business organizations pending closing (DEFM14A pp.71,77-78), so processes and the people running them stayed aligned, giving gap_56 = 0 despite full board/officer turnover. Because no structural transfer gap is documented, gap_mitigated = NA; the absence of any TSA/shared-services agreement is noted but not needed since the whole entity transferred intact.

gemini.rationale: The evidence explicitly states that ESL as a whole corporate entity, including its subsidiaries and operating segments, was acquired intact without any carve-outs at closing. Therefore, the products (T4) and the operational processes (T5) transferred together, resulting in no gap_45. Similarly, the organization and employees (T6) transferred alongside the operations, resulting in no gap_56.

grok.rationale: The reverse triangular merger transferred ESL as a whole corporate entity — stock, subsidiaries, and all three technical-capability segments — intact to TransDigm with no segment carve-outs, so customer-facing products (T4) and the operational processes that produce them (T5) crossed together (DEFM14A pp. 1, 30-31). At closing the workforce remained as continuing ESL employees under contractual compensation/benefits/service-credit protections, while only the board and named officers were replaced by TransDigm designees; thus T5 processes and the T6 organization that runs them were not structurally separated (8-K 2019-03-14 Item 5.02; DEFM14A pp. 77-78). No transition-services or shared-services agreement is described among the transaction documents, but none was required for alignment because the full operating entity moved as one.
